handback.t:
STATUS: highest round completed = R83 (all in C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\RD-LOG.md; local commits only, nothing pushed; I am sole committer; `cargo test --release --lib` = 351 passed before building and after the Rust changes). RD-LOG-B.md did not exist yet, so nothing from Team B was integrated.

Note: `cargo` on PATH is the Cargo-AI npm shim; use `export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"`. My first commit (R70) also swept in ~160 previously untracked src/bin files from earlier sessions.

KEPT (all opt-in or advice only, defaults unchanged)
- R66 item-disjoint verbal splits (the validity hole is fixed): vocab=BGE confirmed (pooled +.26, W/L 20/3, p=5e-4).
- R67 pre-registered blind retest on a fresh pool: vocab BGE +.20 (10/1). cloze_mix and analogies-BGE stay NOT CONFIRMED.
- R68 random-expression generator for identity claims (1,440 true / 960 near / 1,440 diff): the strict verifier has 0 false rejects and near_rej .978.
- R69 strict probe range for the second variable extended with +-100 and +-1000: near_rej .979 -> .992 (12/0 wins, p=.0005) on fresh seeds; true_acc and diff_rej unchanged at 1.000.
- R70 `flatq::suggest_flat_fast` and `FLAT_HNSW_CROSSOVER_N` added. Finding: the H6 table in `suggest_tier` is 2-4.5x too optimistic for block-fp16 and int8+rerank versus FlatIndex. With fast kernels exact f32 is the fastest flat tier: 634 us / 4.4 ms / 50.7 ms at N=1e4 / 1e5 / 1e6.
- R72 `tok_*` cost axes added to `gate.py` (lower is better). Length-aware context re-rank with lam=.1 passes the gate but the effect is small (real -2.4% tokens, ctx_hit unchanged).
- R73-R74 registry token cost measured: the whole catalog is 27,959 estimated tokens (34,629 by cl100k). Injecting top-3/5/10 costs 72/123/265 estimated tokens (95/159/334 by cl100k), about -99.5% to -99.7% for top-3/5. Retrieval hit@1/3/5/10 on 124 queries (including 47 blind Q3 queries I wrote from sampled entries, so lexical overlap is optimistic): .82/.90/.94/.96. Agent entries average 31 estimated tokens. No policy variant (dedup, adaptive alpha, dense) was significantly better than plain hybrid.
- R76/R79 tokens forwarded to the LLM, with kNN-router savings: battery 24.4 -> 5.9 per item (-76%); novel phrasing 11.4/12.1 -> 3.3/3.6 (-70%). Keyword rules show similar token savings only by answering 5% (battery) to 60% (novel phrasing) of non-tool requests with a tool.
- R80 abstain knob for the kNN router (forward to the LLM when top vote share < tau=.6): wrong-tool answers drop 5x on dev and 3.5x on blind, at +14% to +42% forwarded tokens. This is a trade, not a free win; n is small (84 / 60 requests).
- R77 per-store retrieval-budget table: k=1 is enough on easy stores (-80% tokens versus k=5); hard/noisy stores need k>=5.
- R75 lookup latency breakdown (measurement only): query encoding takes 2.7 ms at 4 threads, which dominates for N<=1e4 (about 5.0 ms at 1 thread, 2.2 ms at 8). With d=192 the f32 scan is 284 us at N=1e4, 2.2x faster than d=384.
- R81 token estimate calibration against cl100k: the 1.33 x words rule is accurate for prose (-1%) but undercounts registry entries by 19% and battery questions by 29%.

REJECTED / NOT CONFIRMED
- R71 and R78: query-adaptive context size (score-gap/ratio cutoffs and dense-BM25 agreement) lies on or below the fixed-k frontier on real text.
- R82: the R63 retrieval profile at top-5 raises real context tokens +6% at equal hit; cutting k to 3-4 loses real-text hit.
- R83: profile + length term lam=.2 passes the gate but lam was picked on HELD/CONF, so it is NOT CONFIRMED.
- Registry policy arms (R74) and BGE-plain cloze (R66) were not better.
- Cross-turn context dedup could not be measured: the real query streams have no repeated queries.
- Dynamic int8 quantisation of the encoder was not tested (needs the `onnx` package).

Loud limits: the real-store hit rate is only .45 at k=5, so context size trades hit for tokens at about .6 hit per 1000 tokens, and nothing I tried bends that frontier. Quality of selection from a trimmed injected line is not measured. Token counts are proxies: 1.33 x words, and cl100k as a stand-in for Claude's tokenizer.

NEXT IDEAS
- Per-agent token accounting inside real multi-agent sessions, which needs real traffic or a recorded session.
- Query-embedding memo hit rate on recorded queries.
- A Rust helper for per-store k selection.
- A fresh real-text seed set so the R83 lam can be tuned on tune seeds and confirmed on separate held-out seeds.
- Integrate Team B's wins once RD-LOG-B.md appears.
